Subject: Post-demo recap + proposed next tests (Redwood vs hyperscaler)

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today  great to meet the Luminar team. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Summary: showed hosted API, Dedicated sizing options, and a short comparison of output quality we saw on your exemplar prompts.
- Differentiators we highlighted: production-first runtime, prefix/KV cache for chat, transparent unit cost levers (batching/quant profiles), and fallback policies for availability.

Proposed next tests to validate model quality and regressions vs hyperscaler: 
1) Run your 200 prompt eval set (we requested the prompt CSV) against: a) your current cloud endpoint (hyperscaler), b) Redwood hosted default model, c) Redwood quantized variant on Dedicated.
2) Measure: semantic accuracy, hallucination rate (false facts), and response style stability. We'll also instrument latency and token-cost.
3) Timeline: we can run baseline tests and share a first report within 3 business days once we have the prompt set + sample traffic patterns.

Can you confirm you can share the prompt CSV and whether we should mirror any realtime constraints (token caps / truncation) for the test?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa  appreciate the clear recap. Priya and I spoke internally; we're aligned to run the eval. A couple of clarifications: 

- We'll share the prompt CSV (200 prompts) by end of day tomorrow. It includes a mix of product QA queries, user support scenarios, and a handful of long-context threads.
- Hyperscaler endpoint details: we will run it ourselves and share logs, but if you can also run a side-by-side against your hosted API that would be ideal.
- Our primary signal is hallucination rate (we have a small ground-truth set of 45 prompts). We also care about response consistency for follow-up prompts in a chat flow.

One ask: can Rishi lead the eval design on your side so we have matching tokenization/truncation rules? Also wondering if Redwood's default hosted model can be pinned to a stable version during testing.

Subject: Eval runner + initial quality notes (attached prompt set)

Attaching the prompt CSV you promised (eval-prompt-set.csv)  thanks for sending. Below are initial notes from the first pass we ran against a 50-sample subset: 

- Observations vs hyperscaler default endpoint: Redwood hosted default matched or exceeded semantic accuracy on 34/50 samples. Hallucination rate: hyperscaler 0.18 vs Redwood hosted 0.12 on the subset (measured against your ground-truth).
- Failure modes: hyperscaler occasionally truncated long conversational context leading to incomplete answers; we saw that less frequently with Redwood due to our context caching/KV handling (this is preliminary).
- Latency: median per-response latency was comparable (Redwood 220ms vs hyperscaler 210ms for the 50-sample run) when both endpoints used similar compute. Dedicated quantized variant saw slightly higher tail latency but lower per-token cost.

Attached: eval-prompt-set.csv (subset), and a short run log. Next steps I propose: 
1) Run full 200-prompt batch with pinned hosted model + your hyperscaler run.
2) Run the 20 high-risk regression prompts with increased sampling (beam/temperature sweep) to reproduce hallucinations.
3) Produce a short report with per-prompt diff and counts of hallucinations, semantic-score histograms, and token-cost estimates.

I'll drop the runner and scoring script into the shared Drive folder and post a link.

-Rishi
